classes.objetivo: Reconocer en un ensayo breve la tesis, las frases temáticas y la conclusión, y saber qué función cumple cada parte.

ensenanza.en: A strong introduction hooks the reader and ends with a thesis statement, the sentence that tells us exactly what the essay will defend.
ensenanza.es: Una buena introducción engancha al lector y termina con un enunciado de tesis, la frase que dice exactamente qué defenderá el ensayo.
ensenanza.nota: La tesis suele ocupar la última frase de la introducción.

ensenanza.en: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence, so a reader who skims only first lines still sees what the essay argues.
ensenanza.es: Cada párrafo de desarrollo abre con una frase temática, así que un lector que solo ojea las primeras líneas ve igualmente lo que el ensayo sostiene.
ensenanza.nota: Argues que + oración: el ensayo toma una postura.

ensenanza.en: The rest of the paragraph supports that opening claim with evidence, examples and reasons, each one linked to the point above.
ensenanza.es: El resto del párrafo respalda esa afirmación inicial con pruebas, ejemplos y razones, cada una enlazada con el punto anterior.
ensenanza.nota: Support (verbo) = dar pruebas o razones a favor de una idea.

ensenanza.en: Good writers signpost their structure with phrases such as in the first place or by contrast, so readers never lose the thread.
ensenanza.es: Los buenos autores señalizan su estructura con expresiones como «en primer lugar» o «por el contrario», y así los lectores nunca pierden el hilo.
ensenanza.nota: Signpost funciona como verbo: marca el camino al lector.

ensenanza.en: A forceful conclusion restates the thesis in fresh words and can round off the essay without introducing a new argument.
ensenanza.es: Una conclusión contundente reformula la tesis con palabras nuevas y puede cerrar el ensayo sin introducir un argumento nuevo.
ensenanza.nota: Restates = dice lo mismo con otras palabras; round off = cerrar de forma redonda.

ensenanza.en: Before writing, draw up an outline to build a case for one position, because a plan shows at once which point is missing.
ensenanza.es: Antes de escribir, elabora un esquema para argumentar a favor de una postura, porque un plan muestra enseguida qué punto falta.
ensenanza.nota: Build a case for + sustantivo: construir los argumentos de una postura.

explicacion.titulo: Anatomía de un ensayo: tesis, frases temáticas y cierre
explicacion.texto: Un ensayo de cinco párrafos tiene una estructura predecible. La introducción presenta el tema y termina con la thesis statement: la postura que todo el texto defiende. Cada body paragraph empieza con una topic sentence que anuncia su idea central, y el resto la supports con datos y ejemplos. La conclusión restates la tesis con otras palabras y cierra sin ideas nuevas. Si lees la tesis y la primera frase de cada párrafo, obtienes el outline completo del ensayo.

formula.texto: Cities should ban cars from their centres.
formula.nota: tesis: la postura que se defiende

formula.texto: First, cars make the air dirtier.
Figures from three cities show it.
formula.nota: apoyo: datos que respaldan la idea

formula.texto: To sum up, centres are better without cars.

filas.texto: la postura que defiende el ensayo
retoma la tesis sin ideas nuevas

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The conclusion restate the thesis in fresh words.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The conclusion restates the thesis in fresh words.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con sujeto singular (the conclusion) el verbo en presente lleva -s: restates.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The topic sentence announces about the main idea.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The topic sentence announces the main idea.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Announce es transitivo: no lleva about; se dice announce the idea.

situacion.contexto: Leo y Mia repasan juntos el ensayo que Mia va a entregar.

dialogo.texto: Your introduction is good, but where is the thesis statement?
dialogo.traduccion: Tu introducción es buena, pero ¿dónde está el enunciado de la tesis?

dialogo.texto: It is the last sentence: I will argue that libraries should stay open at night.
dialogo.traduccion: Es la última frase: defenderé que las bibliotecas deberían seguir abiertas por la noche.

dialogo.texto: Right. And each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence, so the outline is clear.
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. Y cada párrafo de desarrollo abre con una frase temática, así que el esquema es claro.

dialogo.texto: I also wrote a forceful conclusion that restates the thesis in fresh words.
dialogo.traduccion: También escribí una conclusión contundente que reformula la tesis con palabras nuevas.

dialogo.texto: Good. Now signpost the second point, so readers never lose the thread.
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. Ahora señaliza el segundo punto, para que los lectores nunca pierdan el hilo.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué le recomienda Leo a Mia al final?

opciones.es: Que señalice mejor el segundo punto para guiar al lector.
Que cambie la tesis por una frase más corta.
Que elimine la conclusión porque repite la tesis.

item.feedback: Leo le pide que señalice el segundo punto con expresiones que guíen al lector («signpost the second point»).

guiada.consigna: ¿Cuál es la frase temática de este párrafo?
guiada.texto: School gardens teach pupils to care for living things. Pupils who grow vegetables often try new foods at lunch, and teachers report calmer lessons after garden sessions. Gardens also bring neighbours into the school.
opciones: School gardens teach pupils to care for living things.
Pupils who grow vegetables often try new foods at lunch.
Gardens also bring neighbours into the school.
guiada.feedback: La frase temática anuncia la idea del párrafo; las demás la apoyan con un dato y con una consecuencia.
guiada.pista: Es la frase que abre el párrafo y resume su idea.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «La introducción termina con un enunciado de tesis.»
guiada.texto: A good introduction presents the subject. It ends with a thesis ___ that tells readers exactly what the essay will defend.
guiada.feedback: Thesis statement es el término para la frase que fija la postura del ensayo, normalmente al final de la introducción.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Cada párrafo de desarrollo abre con una frase temática.»
guiada.respuesta: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence
guiada.feedback: Body paragraph es el sujeto; opens with a topic sentence describe cómo empieza.
guiada.pista: El sujeto es Each body paragraph.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué hace la segunda frase respecto a la primera del párrafo?
practica.texto: Uniforms save families money. A typical family spends less on school clothes when one uniform replaces many different clothes, and the school's own survey found that eight in ten parents agreed. Uniforms also reduce arguments about what to wear.
opciones: It backs up the opening claim with an example and a figure.
It restates the claim in new words without adding anything.
It brings in a counterargument that the writer will answer later.
It signals that the paragraph is moving on to a new topic.
practica.feedback: La segunda frase aporta un ejemplo concreto y una cifra de una encuesta: respalda la afirmación inicial.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué la profesora lee solo las primeras frases.
practica.audio: When I read a student essay, I start with the last sentence of the introduction, because that is where the thesis usually sits. Then I read only the first sentence of each body paragraph. If those sentences, put together, tell a clear story, the outline is sound. If they jump from idea to idea, I already know where the essay needs work, before I have read a single example.
opciones: To test whether the topic sentences form a clear outline.
To save time, because examples are rarely important in an essay.
To reach the conclusion before she reads the thesis.
To check that every paragraph begins with a signpost.
practica.feedback: Las primeras frases de cada párrafo, leídas juntas, muestran si el esquema del ensayo es claro.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la parte del ensayo a la que pertenece.
pares: Many schools now face a difficult choice.
I will argue that homework should be shorter.
Second, short tasks help pupils to sleep.
To sum up, less homework means better learning.
practica.feedback: Cada frase ocupa un lugar distinto: apertura, tesis, frase temática y conclusión.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué frase del ensayo contiene la tesis?
evaluacion.texto: Many towns now struggle with heat, dust and constant noise. I will argue that every town should plant more trees along its streets. First, trees make the air in the streets far cooler. Measurements in three towns show that summer temperatures fell by two degrees where trees were planted. Second, a shaded street is better for trade. Shops on tree-lined streets reported more customers, because people stopped to look at the windows. To sum up, the evidence suggests that streets with trees are cooler, quieter and busier. Towns that hesitate are choosing the problem over the solution.
opciones: Every town should plant more trees along its streets.
Heat, dust and noise are common problems in towns.
Summer temperatures fell by two degrees in three towns.
Hesitant towns are choosing the problem over the solution.
evaluacion.feedback: La tesis es la postura que defiende todo el ensayo y se anuncia con «I will argue that»; las demás frases describen el contexto, aportan datos o cierran.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el párrafo final y elige qué hace el autor con el coste de abrir por la noche.
opciones: He concedes the objection, but argues that the evidence still favours his thesis.
He uses the cost to show that his own thesis is unrealistic.
He offers the cost as one more reason to open libraries at night.
He accepts that only a few branches matter, so he gives up his thesis.
evaluacion.feedback: El autor admite que abrir de noche cuesta dinero («Of course…»), pero sostiene que las pruebas de los proyectos piloto siguen respaldando su tesis; no la abandona ni usa el coste como argumento a favor.
evaluacion.audio: The final paragraph of the essay reads like this. Libraries that close at six serve only those who finish work early, and the readers who need them most are left outside. Of course, opening at night costs money, and I do not claim that every branch must do it. But the pilot schemes leave little room for doubt: where doors stayed open, membership rose by a third. Councils that refuse to look at those figures are defending a timetable, not their readers.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «En el último párrafo el autor retoma la tesis con otras palabras.»
evaluacion.texto: The essay ends with a short paragraph. In it, the writer ___ the thesis in fresh words instead of copying it from the introduction.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena conclusión restates la tesis: dice lo mismo con otras palabras y sin añadir ideas nuevas.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe la frase de tesis de un ensayo sobre el horario de los colegios.
evaluacion.texto: Tema: los colegios deberían empezar más tarde. Escribe una frase de tesis con una fórmula como I will argue that… y una razón.
evaluacion.respuesta: I will argue that schools should start later, because teenagers learn better when they have slept enough.
aceptadas: This essay argues that schools should begin later in the morning, since tired pupils cannot learn properly.
I will argue that school should start later, as teenagers concentrate better after a full night of sleep.
evaluacion.feedback: Una tesis clara combina una fórmula de postura, la idea que se defiende y una razón breve.

evidencias: schools should start later in the morning

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué cabe esperar del resto del ensayo a partir de esta introducción?
repaso.texto: Sport is important in modern life. Many people play it and many more watch it on television. Some players earn millions, while others train in the rain for nothing. In this essay I am going to talk about sport.
opciones: A description of sport in general, with no position to defend.
A detailed attack on professional players and their salaries.
A strong case against watching sport on television.
A comparison of how much famous and ordinary players train.
repaso.feedback: «I am going to talk about sport» anuncia un tema, no una postura: sin tesis, lo esperable es un texto descriptivo que no defiende nada.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «El autor quiere argumentar a favor de horarios más tardíos.»
repaso.texto: The writer wants to ___ a case for later school hours, so every paragraph supports a single position.
repaso.feedback: Build a case for describe reunir razones y pruebas en favor de una postura.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Un esquema muestra de un vistazo qué punto falta.»
repaso.respuesta: An outline shows at a glance which point is missing
repaso.feedback: Which point is missing es una pregunta indirecta: el verbo va después del sujeto.
aceptadas: At a glance an outline shows which point is missing

classes.objetivo: Enlazar frases sin repetir palabras con this/such, the former/the latter, the same y respectively, y señalar hacia atrás y hacia delante.

ensenanza.en: Shop owners and residents asked for parking and quiet respectively, so the former wanted access and the latter wanted peace.
ensenanza.es: Los comerciantes y los vecinos pidieron estacionamiento y tranquilidad respectivamente, así que los primeros querían acceso y los segundos paz.
ensenanza.nota: Respectively empareja dos listas en el mismo orden; the former y the latter distinguen dos elementos.

ensenanza.en: The council introduced a ban on cars; such a decision was unpopular at first, yet the aforementioned ban has since reduced noise.
ensenanza.es: El municipio introdujo una prohibición de autos; una decisión así fue impopular al principio, pero la mencionada prohibición ha reducido el ruido.
ensenanza.nota: Such a + sustantivo resume y califica la idea anterior; aforementioned es formal.

ensenanza.en: The writer cut the report to one page, thereby saving her readers time, and in doing so she kept her argument clear.
ensenanza.es: La autora redujo el informe a una página, con lo cual ahorró tiempo a sus lectores, y al hacerlo mantuvo claro su argumento.
ensenanza.nota: Thereby + gerundio añade el resultado; in doing so retoma la acción anterior.

ensenanza.en: The buses were late on Monday and Tuesday by ten and twenty minutes respectively, and the same applies to the trams.
ensenanza.es: Los autobuses llegaron tarde el lunes y el martes con diez y veinte minutos respectivamente, y lo mismo se aplica a los tranvías.
ensenanza.nota: The same applies to + sustantivo evita repetir toda la frase.

ensenanza.en: The previous paragraph named two causes; the following points explain them, thereby guiding readers backwards and then forwards.
ensenanza.es: El párrafo anterior nombraba dos causas; los puntos siguientes las explican, con lo cual guían al lector hacia atrás y luego hacia delante.
ensenanza.nota: Previous mira hacia atrás; following mira hacia delante.

ensenanza.en: Pupils should respect teachers; by the same token, teachers should respect pupils, and in this respect the aforementioned rules are fair.
ensenanza.es: Los alumnos deben respetar a los profesores; por la misma razón, los profesores deben respetar a los alumnos, y en este sentido las normas mencionadas son justas.
ensenanza.nota: By the same token introduce un paralelo; in this respect limita el comentario a un aspecto.

explicacion.titulo: Señalar hacia atrás y hacia delante sin repetir
explicacion.texto: Para no repetir palabras, el inglés escrito enlaza las frases con referencias. This/such a + sustantivo resume la idea anterior (such a decision); the former y the latter distinguen dos elementos citados, y respectively los empareja en el mismo orden. Con the same applies to y by the same token evitas repetir una frase entera; in doing so y thereby añaden una consecuencia. Hacia delante apuntan the following points. Regla de oro: si hay dos posibles antecedentes, repite el sustantivo para que la referencia sea clara.

formula.texto: The council banned cars from the centre.

formula.nota: referencia: resume y califica la idea

formula.texto: and in doing so it changed the street.
formula.nota: in doing so: retoma la acción

filas.texto: Such a decision is rarely popular.
The former pollute; the latter block.
dos listas en el mismo orden

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Cars and bikes cause problems: the former pollute the air and the later block the pavements.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Cars and bikes cause problems: the former pollute the air and the latter block the pavements.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: The latter (el segundo) no es the later (más tarde): se escribe con -tt-.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Such decision is rarely popular at first.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Such a decision is rarely popular at first.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con un sustantivo contable singular, such lleva el artículo a: such a decision.

situacion.contexto: Carlos y Sara revisan un informe escolar sobre el transporte.

dialogo.texto: The report names two reasons for the long queues, the timetable and the room. The former is easy to fix, but the latter is not.
dialogo.traduccion: El informe nombra dos razones de las colas largas, el horario y la sala. El primero es fácil de arreglar, pero la segunda no.

dialogo.texto: I agree. And the previous paragraph repeats the word queue six times.
dialogo.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo. Y el párrafo anterior repite la palabra cola seis veces.

dialogo.texto: We could write the word queue once and then use a reference, thereby saving space.
dialogo.traduccion: Podríamos escribir la palabra cola una vez y luego usar una referencia, con lo cual ahorramos espacio.

dialogo.texto: Good idea. The same applies to the word report. Let us fix both before the following points.
dialogo.traduccion: Buena idea. Lo mismo se aplica a la palabra informe. Arreglemos ambas antes de los puntos siguientes.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué problema detectan en el párrafo anterior?

opciones.es: Que repite la misma palabra varias veces.
Que nombra el horario y la sala sin decir cuál es más grave.
Que olvida anunciar los puntos siguientes.

item.feedback: Sara dice que el párrafo anterior repite la palabra queue seis veces; por eso proponen usar referencias.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué versión evita la repetición con una referencia correcta?
guiada.texto: Original: The council closed the market square. The council's closure of the market square upset the traders.
opciones: The council closed the market square. Such a decision upset the traders.
The council closed the market square. The former upset the traders.
The council closed the market square. Respectively upset the traders.
guiada.feedback: Such a decision resume la acción anterior y la califica; the former exige dos elementos previos y respectively exige dos listas.
guiada.pista: Busca la referencia que resume la idea anterior en una frase nominal.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El primero contamina el aire, mientras que el segundo no.»
guiada.texto: Cars and trams both serve the centre. The former pollutes the air, whereas the ___ does not.
guiada.feedback: The latter se refiere al segundo de dos elementos ya citados; aquí, los tranvías.
guiada.pista: Se refiere al segundo de dos elementos.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Se cancelaron las clases, y lo mismo se aplica al deporte.»
guiada.respuesta: Lessons were cancelled and the same applies to sport
guiada.feedback: The same applies to + sustantivo extiende lo dicho a otro elemento sin repetirlo.
guiada.pista: El verbo applies va con to.

practica.texto: Sara and Tom were asked to lead the two workshops, on music and on photography respectively. The former was shy, and the latter, who had never taught before, was nervous. Such a choice might seem odd, but both did well.
opciones: Tom, the latter of the two.
Sara, the former of the two.
Sara and Tom together, since they shared both workshops.
Nobody, because the latter was too nervous to teach.
practica.feedback: Respectively empareja música con Sara y fotografía con Tom; Tom es «the latter», el segundo nombrado.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué el compromiso agradó a los padres.
practica.audio: My brother and I argued about two holiday plans, a week by the sea and a week in the mountains. The former was my choice and the latter was his. In the end, we chose neither, but such a compromise pleased our parents, who had feared a long argument. The following summer we did the same, and this time nobody complained.
opciones: It spared them a long argument between their children.
It was cheaper than either of the original plans.
It allowed them to spend a week in the mountains.
It proved that both children had grown up.
practica.feedback: Los padres temían una larga discusión; el compromiso se la ahorró. El texto no habla de dinero ni de madurez.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la función de su referencia.
pares: Empareja dos listas en el mismo orden
Se refiere al primero de dos citados
Such a decision is rarely popular.
Resume y califica la idea anterior
practica.feedback: Cada referencia cumple una función distinta: emparejar, distinguir, resumir y anunciar.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué reprocha la locutora a la autora sobre las dos explicaciones.
evaluacion.audio: The report gives two explanations for the fall in sales, the new supermarket and the bad weather. The former is easy to measure, since the supermarket opened in March; the latter is not, because weather data for the region is incomplete. The author nonetheless blames the supermarket, and in doing so she gives more weight to the evidence she happens to have. Such a choice is understandable, but it is open to question. By the same token, the report ignores the third factor mentioned on its own last page, the rise in fuel prices, which may well account for a good part of the drop.
opciones: Favouring the explanation she can measure over one she cannot.
Overlooking that the supermarket opened too late to affect sales.
Ignoring the weather data that the report itself supplies.
Blaming the weather when the supermarket was the real cause.
evaluacion.feedback: La autora prefiere la explicación que puede medir («the former»), aunque sea discutible; además omite un tercer factor que aparece en su propia última página.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué reescritura elimina la repetición sin crear ambigüedad?
evaluacion.texto: Original: The report names two causes of the delay, the strike and the snow. The strike began on Monday, and the snow began on Wednesday. The report says the strike was short, and the report says the snow was heavy.
opciones: The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; the former began on Monday and the latter on Wednesday, short and heavy respectively.
The report names two causes. It began on Monday and on Wednesday, and it was short and heavy, as the report itself says in this respect.
The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; the latter began on Monday and the former on Wednesday, short and heavy respectively.
The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; both began on Monday, short and heavy respectively.
evaluacion.feedback: Solo la versión con the former, the latter y respectively en el orden correcto mantiene la correspondencia (huelga-lunes-corta, nieve-miércoles-intensa).

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Una decisión así dejó a muchos comerciantes sin ingresos.»
evaluacion.texto: The council closed the market for a week without any warning. ___ a decision left many traders without an income.
evaluacion.feedback: Such a + sustantivo califica la decisión ya mencionada y evita repetir toda la frase.

evaluacion.consigna: Une las dos ideas sin repetir palabras: usa such a… y respectively.
evaluacion.texto: Ideas: el colegio cerró la biblioteca durante los exámenes; los alumnos se quejaron de la falta de espacio y los profesores de la falta de libros. Escríbelo en dos frases sin repetir palabras, con una referencia que resuma el cierre y respectively.
evaluacion.respuesta: The school closed the library during the exams. Such a decision upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and of books respectively.
aceptadas: The school closed its library during the exams. Such a measure upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and of books respectively.
The school closed the library for the exams, and such a move upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and the lack of books respectively.
evaluacion.feedback: Una referencia como such a decision resume el cierre y respectively empareja cada grupo con su queja en el mismo orden.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué opina la editora de las dos mitades del borrador?
repaso.texto: Dear Carlos, the draft reads well, but the same word, plan, opens six sentences on the second page. Replacing some of them with such a measure or this approach would help, although you should check that each one points clearly to the previous sentence. In this respect, the latter half of the draft is better than the former. Best wishes, Mia.
opciones: The second half handles its references better than the first.
The first half is clearer, because it uses fewer references.
Both parts need the same correction for repeating one word.
She sees nothing to improve in either part of the draft.
repaso.feedback: «The latter half is better than the former» significa que la segunda mitad (latter) es mejor que la primera (former).

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Lo mismo se aplica a las entrevistas con los profesores.»
repaso.texto: Only fifty pupils answered the survey. The same ___ to the interviews with teachers, which reached just six people.
repaso.feedback: The same applies to + sustantivo extiende lo dicho a otro caso sin repetirlo.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «En este sentido, los dos informes difieren mucho.»
repaso.respuesta: In this respect the two reports differ greatly
repaso.feedback: In this respect limita la comparación a un aspecto concreto.
aceptadas: The two reports differ greatly in this respect

classes.objetivo: Leer un borrador y localizar repeticiones, referencias ambiguas, saltos lógicos, frases irrelevantes y contradicciones, nombrando cada problema.

vocabulario.es: non sequitur, conclusión que no se deduce
antecedente (a lo que remite un pronombre)

ensenanza.en: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.
ensenanza.es: Un borrador suele ser repetitivo: el mismo sustantivo abre cada frase, y el lector oye un eco en lugar de un argumento.
ensenanza.nota: Repetitive describe un texto que insiste con las mismas palabras.

ensenanza.en: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.
ensenanza.es: En la frase «Ana le dijo a Mia que ella llegaba tarde», el pronombre es ambiguo, pues su antecedente podría ser cualquiera de las dos.
ensenanza.nota: El antecedente es la palabra a la que remite un pronombre.

ensenanza.en: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.
ensenanza.es: Un autor que saca conclusiones precipitadas deja un salto lógico, y el lector sigue sin tener claro el razonamiento.
ensenanza.nota: Jumps to a conclusion = concluye sin pasos intermedios.

ensenanza.en: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.
ensenanza.es: Un párrafo sobre autobuses escolares no debería irse por las ramas hablando de vacaciones, porque una frase irrelevante debilita la idea.
ensenanza.nota: Irrelevant = no tiene que ver con el tema del párrafo.

ensenanza.en: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.
ensenanza.es: Cuando una frase contradice a otra, el párrafo se viene abajo, y un non sequitur, que no se deduce de nada, hace el mismo daño.
ensenanza.nota: Contradicts lleva objeto directo: contradicts the first sentence, sin to.

ensenanza.en: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.
ensenanza.es: Una redacción vaga, con palabras como «cosas», deja al lector sin tener claro el punto, así que sustitúyela por el sustantivo exacto.
ensenanza.nota: Vague wording = palabras demasiado generales; se opone a precise.

explicacion.titulo: Diagnosticar un borrador: localizar y nombrar el fallo
explicacion.texto: Un borrador con problemas de coherencia muestra cinco síntomas. Repetición: la misma palabra abre todas las frases. Referencia ambigua: un pronombre puede remitir a dos antecedentes. Salto lógico: pasas de una idea a otra sin la razón que las une (jumps to a conclusion, non sequitur). Frase irrelevante: va por las ramas. Contradicción: una frase niega otra. Lee como un lector que no sabe nada y formula tu nota con lugar + tipo de problema + because + razón.

formula.texto: because its antecedent could be Ana or Mia.

filas.texto: The plan… The plan… The plan…
Ana told Mia she was late.
A holiday in a report on buses.
It is cheap. It costs a lot.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The sentence is ambiguous because we do not know to who she refers.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The sentence is ambiguous because we do not know who she refers to.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En una pregunta indirecta la preposición va al final: who she refers to.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The second sentence is contradicting to the first one.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The second sentence contradicts the first one.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Contradict es transitivo y no lleva to; además se usa en presente simple.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom leen en voz alta el borrador de un informe sobre el transporte escolar.

dialogo.texto: Listen to this: The plan is good. The plan is cheap. The plan is easy. It is repetitive, is it not?
dialogo.traduccion: Escucha esto: El plan es bueno. El plan es barato. El plan es fácil. Es repetitivo, ¿no?

dialogo.texto: Yes. And here, Ana told Mia she was late. The pronoun is ambiguous, because its antecedent could be either girl.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Y aquí, Ana le dijo a Mia que llegaba tarde. El pronombre es ambiguo, porque su antecedente podría ser cualquiera de las dos.

dialogo.texto: The last line is worse. The writer jumps to a conclusion: sales rose, so the plan failed.
dialogo.traduccion: La última línea es peor. El autor saca una conclusión precipitada: las ventas subieron, así que el plan fracasó.

dialogo.texto: That is a logical gap. We should ask for the missing step before we mark the draft as finished.
dialogo.traduccion: Eso es un salto lógico. Deberíamos pedir el paso que falta antes de dar el borrador por terminado.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué fallo señala Tom en la frase «las ventas subieron, así que el plan fracasó»?

opciones.es: Un salto lógico: falta el paso que une la causa con la conclusión.
Una contradicción con la primera frase del borrador.
Una repetición de la misma palabra en cada frase.

item.feedback: Tom llama «logical gap» a ese salto: el autor concluye sin explicar el paso intermedio.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué problema principal tiene este fragmento del borrador?
guiada.texto: The town is small. The town has a river. The town has a market. The town has a school.
opciones: It is repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence.
It is ambiguous: each pronoun could refer to two things.
It contradicts itself about the size of the town.
guiada.feedback: Las tres frases empiezan por «The town» y no aportan una progresión: el problema es la repetición.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Palabras como «cosas» son vagas: no dan nada concreto que imaginar.»
guiada.texto: Words such as things and stuff are ___, because they give readers nothing exact to picture. A precise noun is always better.
guiada.feedback: Vague describe una palabra demasiado general; la solución es sustituirla por el sustantivo exacto.
guiada.pista: Adjetivo que se opone a specific.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «La segunda frase contradice directamente a la primera.»
guiada.respuesta: The second sentence directly contradicts the first one
guiada.feedback: Contradicts es transitivo: va seguido de the first one, sin preposición.
guiada.pista: Directly va justo antes del verbo contradicts.

practica.consigna: Identifica el problema principal del párrafo.
practica.texto: The club needs a new room. The club has three hundred members. The club's members want a room. The club's room is too small, so the club must find another room for the club's members.
opciones: It is repetitive: almost every sentence opens with the same words.
It is ambiguous: the pronouns could refer to two different things.
It contradicts itself about how many members the club has.
It jumps to a conclusion that the figures do not support.
practica.feedback: «The club» abre casi todas las frases y el párrafo suena a eco: el fallo es la repetición.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué solución propone la editora.
practica.audio: A student wrote: The manager told the assistant that he would be promoted. I asked him who would be promoted, and he did not know either. The pronoun he has two possible antecedents, the manager and the assistant, and the reader cannot decide. I suggested repeating the noun. It is a small change, but it removes the doubt completely.
opciones: Replace the pronoun with the noun it stands for.
Delete the sentence because it is irrelevant to the report.
Add a figure to support the claim about the promotion.
Change the verb to a stronger one that the reader remembers.
practica.feedback: La editora propone repetir el sustantivo para eliminar la duda sobre a quién remite «he».

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada fragmento con el problema que presenta.
pares: Ana told Mia she was late.
It is cheap. It costs a lot.
A holiday in a report on buses.
practica.feedback: Cada fragmento ilustra un fallo distinto: salto, ambigüedad, contradicción e irrelevancia.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué problema presenta la frase 4 del borrador?
evaluacion.texto: (1) The school plan for the new bus route is a good plan. (2) The plan was written by the council, and the plan has three stages. (3) Ana told Mia she had to submit it before Friday. (4) The route will be free for pupils, but every pupil must pay two pounds for each journey. (5) My holiday in Spain was wonderful. (6) As a result, the plan is sure to be a success, although no pupil has tried the new route yet. The draft was sent to the head teacher on Monday, together with a short note from the council explaining that the plan would start in September if the pupils agreed.
opciones: It contradicts itself, because a free route cannot charge two pounds a journey.
It is repetitive, because it says the same thing about the route twice.
It is irrelevant, because fares have nothing to do with a route.
It is ambiguous, because the pronoun could refer to two different stages.
evaluacion.feedback: La frase afirma que la ruta será gratuita para los alumnos y a la vez que cada alumno debe pagar dos libras por trayecto: una contradicción interna.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué deja entrever la frase 6 sobre el razonamiento del autor?
evaluacion.texto: (1) The school plan for the new bus route is a good plan. (2) The plan was written by the council, and the plan has three stages. (3) Ana told Mia she had to submit it before Friday. (4) The route will be free for pupils, but every pupil must pay two pounds for each journey. (5) My holiday in Spain was wonderful. (6) As a result, the plan is sure to be a success, although no pupil has tried the new route yet. The draft was sent to the head teacher on Monday, together with a short note from the council explaining that the plan would start in September if the pupils agreed.
opciones: That it reaches a conclusion the earlier sentences do not justify.
That it contradicts the claim that the route will be free.
That it repeats the idea of the first sentence in other words.
That it uses a pronoun whose antecedent cannot be identified.
evaluacion.feedback: La frase concluye que el plan será un éxito aunque nadie ha probado la ruta: es un salto lógico sin apoyo en lo anterior.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El pronombre es ambiguo porque puede referirse a cualquiera de las dos.»
evaluacion.texto: In the sentence Sara told Luna that she had won, the pronoun is ___, because it could refer to either girl.
evaluacion.feedback: Un pronombre con dos antecedentes posibles es ambiguous: el lector no puede decidir a quién remite.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una nota de edición para la frase 5: nombra el problema y explica por qué.
evaluacion.texto: Frase del borrador, en un informe sobre transporte escolar: «My holiday in Spain was wonderful.» Escribe en inglés una nota breve: nombra el problema y explica la razón con because.
evaluacion.respuesta: This sentence is irrelevant, because a holiday in Spain has nothing to do with a school bus route.
aceptadas: This sentence is off the topic, since a holiday in Spain does not belong in a report on school buses.
The sentence is irrelevant because a holiday in Spain has no connection with the bus route.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena nota de edición nombra el problema (irrelevant) y da una razón concreta con because.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué crítica hace el editor del tercer párrafo?
opciones: It leaves a logical gap between falling attendance and the timetable's failure.
It repeats one noun until the reader hears only an echo.
It contradicts what the second paragraph said about attendance.
It relies on vague words in place of the exact nouns.
repaso.feedback: El editor señala que se pasa de «attendance fell» a «the new timetable is a disaster» sin explicar la conexión: falta un paso lógico.
repaso.audio: Dear Leo, I read your draft twice. Paragraph two is strong, but in the third you move from attendance fell in March to the new timetable is a disaster without explaining why the two are connected, and the final one goes off on a tangent about your holiday. I would keep the facts and add the missing step. Best wishes, Mar.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Un párrafo sobre vacaciones en un informe de autobuses se irá por las ramas.»
repaso.texto: The report is about school buses. A paragraph about holidays would ___ off on a tangent, and the reader would lose the thread.
repaso.feedback: Go off on a tangent significa alejarse del tema principal, como haría un párrafo sobre vacaciones en un informe de autobuses.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «El autor saca una conclusión precipitada sin ninguna prueba.»
repaso.respuesta: The writer jumps to a conclusion without any evidence
repaso.feedback: Jumps to a conclusion describe concluir sin pasos intermedios; without any evidence añade la falta de pruebas.
aceptadas: Without any evidence the writer jumps to a conclusion

classes.objetivo: Escribir un párrafo largo sobre una decisión personal con conectores variados y recortar frases largas sin perder contenido.

vocabulario.es: es cierto que, hay que admitir que

ensenanza.en: A wordy sentence can usually be rewritten as a concise version that keeps every idea and loses half the words.
ensenanza.es: Una frase prolija suele poder reescribirse como una versión concisa que conserva todas las ideas y pierde la mitad de las palabras.
ensenanza.nota: Wordy y concise son opuestos: muchas palabras frente a las justas.

ensenanza.en: To tighten up a draft, cut redundant words such as very, really and basically, which add no information.
ensenanza.es: Para ajustar un borrador, elimina palabras redundantes como very, really y basically, que no añaden información.
ensenanza.nota: Tighten up = hacer el texto más compacto; redundant = sobra.

ensenanza.en: Write because instead of due to the fact that, and decided instead of made a decision: each change is shorter and stronger.
ensenanza.es: Escribe because en lugar de due to the fact that, y decided en lugar de made a decision: cada cambio es más corto y más fuerte.
ensenanza.nota: Un verbo fuerte (decided) sustituye a verbo + sustantivo (made a decision).

ensenanza.en: A verbose opening delays the message, so good writers get to the point in the first sentence.
ensenanza.es: Una apertura verbosa retrasa el mensaje, así que los buenos autores van al grano en la primera frase.
ensenanza.nota: Get to the point = decir lo esencial sin rodeos.

ensenanza.en: I trimmed down the paragraph from twenty words to twelve by deleting every superfluous phrase, and no information was lost.
ensenanza.es: Recorté el párrafo de veinte palabras a doce eliminando cada frase superflua, y no se perdió ninguna información.
ensenanza.nota: Superfluous es formal: algo que sobra y no aporta.

ensenanza.en: Admittedly, the course is expensive; nevertheless, it is worth the cost, because the tutors explain each point clearly.
ensenanza.es: Es cierto que el curso es caro; sin embargo, merece lo que cuesta, porque los tutores explican cada punto con claridad.
ensenanza.nota: Admittedly concede un punto; nevertheless lo contrasta. Los dos conectores varían el ritmo.

explicacion.texto: Escribir bien es escribir y luego recortar. Primero redacta el párrafo completo con conectores variados: admittedly concede un punto y nevertheless o however lo contrasta. Después tighten up: cambia due to the fact that por because, in order to por to y made a decision por decided, y elimina palabras redundantes. Una versión concisa conserva todo el contenido con menos palabras; si al recortar pierdes una idea, has recortado demasiado. Y recuerda: get to the point desde la primera frase.

formula.texto: Due to the fact that it was late,
formula.nota: versión larga: cinco palabras para una idea
verbo fuerte, sin made a decision

filas.texto: una palabra en lugar de cinco

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I made a decision of studying abroad.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Decide + to + verbo base es más corto y natural; «decision of + gerundio» es un calco.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: In order to saving money, I work at weekends.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: To save money, I work at weekends.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de to va el verbo base, no -ing; además se puede quitar in order.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Carlos recortan el párrafo que Sara presentará en clase.

dialogo.texto: Is my paragraph too wordy? I wrote due to the fact that it rained, I made the decision to cancel the picnic.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Mi párrafo es demasiado prolijo? Escribí debido a que llovía, tomé la decisión de cancelar el picnic.

dialogo.texto: Yes. A concise version would be: Because it rained, I decided to cancel the picnic.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Una versión concisa sería: Como llovía, decidí cancelar el picnic.

dialogo.texto: Admittedly, that is shorter. Nevertheless, I do not want to lose the reason.
dialogo.traduccion: Es cierto que es más corto. Sin embargo, no quiero perder la razón.

dialogo.texto: You have not lost it. The reason is still there, and the superfluous words are gone.
dialogo.traduccion: No la has perdido. La razón sigue ahí, y las palabras superfluas han desaparecido.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué teme Sara al recortar su frase?

opciones.es: Perder la razón que explica su decisión.
Que la frase quede demasiado larga.
Que Carlos no entienda el conector.

item.feedback: Sara dice que no quiere perder la razón; Carlos le responde que sigue en la frase y que solo han desaparecido las palabras superfluas.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué versión es más concisa y conserva todo el contenido?
guiada.texto: Original: Due to the fact that the match was cancelled, we made a decision to stay at home.
opciones: The match was cancelled, so we stayed at home.
Because the match was cancelled, we made the decision to stay at home.
The match having been cancelled, it was our decision to remain at home.
guiada.feedback: La versión «The match was cancelled, so we stayed at home» dice lo mismo con la mitad de palabras; las otras conservan frases vacías como made the decision.
guiada.pista: Busca la versión más corta que no pierde ninguna idea.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Ahora digo simplemente que decidí dejarlo.»
guiada.texto: Last spring I made a decision to leave my job. Now I simply say that I ___ to leave it.
guiada.feedback: Decided sustituye a made a decision: un verbo fuerte en lugar de verbo + sustantivo.
guiada.pista: Verbo en pasado que equivale a «tomar una decisión».

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Recorté las frases sin perder ninguna información.»
guiada.respuesta: I trimmed the sentences without losing any information
guiada.feedback: Without + gerundio expresa que el recorte no tuvo coste de contenido.
aceptadas: Without losing any information I trimmed the sentences
guiada.pista: Empieza por I trimmed; without losing va al final.

practica.consigna: ¿Cuál es la versión más concisa que conserva todo el contenido?
practica.texto: It was absolutely and completely essential for us to basically finish the very important project before the final deadline date.
opciones: It was essential to finish the important project before the deadline.
It was essential to finish everything we had planned for that week.
It was essential to finish the important project.
Completing the project was absolutely essential before the final deadline date.
practica.feedback: Elimina absolutely, completely, basically, very y date, pero conserva lo esencial: terminar el proyecto importante antes del plazo.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué logró la alumna al recortar su introducción.
practica.audio: My tutor returned my essay with one comment: get to the point. My introduction had four sentences of background before the thesis, and two of them were superfluous. I cut them, then replaced due to the fact that with because, and my opening dropped from sixty words to thirty. The content was the same. The essay simply read as though it had been written by someone who respected the reader's time.
opciones: It kept every idea and respected the reader's time.
It removed the thesis, which was the most superfluous part.
It raised her marks, because the essay became much shorter.
It gave the tutor more background to judge her argument.
practica.feedback: La alumna redujo la introducción a la mitad sin perder contenido; el texto no menciona ninguna nota ni que se eliminara la tesis.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión larga con su sustitución más concisa.
pares: Se sustituye por una sola palabra: because
Basta con un adverbio de tiempo
practica.feedback: Cada expresión tiene una versión breve: una conjunción, un infinitivo, un verbo fuerte y un adverbio.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la narradora sobre su mensaje largo.
evaluacion.audio: Last year I wrote an email to my landlord that ran to three paragraphs. I explained, at length and with great feeling, that due to the fact that the heating had broken down, I had been forced to make the decision to move in with my brother. He never replied. When I showed the email to a friend, she asked me what I wanted. A repair, I said. Then write that, she answered. I trimmed the message to four lines, and the heating was fixed within two days. Admittedly, the short version felt less generous to me. Nevertheless, it worked far better.
opciones: That its length hid her request and probably explains the silence.
That the landlord is too busy to read any message about repairs.
That her friend found the long version more convincing than the short one.
That an emotional tone always persuades landlords to act quickly.
evaluacion.feedback: La amiga le hizo ver que lo que quería (una reparación) se perdía entre tantas palabras; al recortar, el problema se resolvió en dos días.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué versión ajusta mejor la frase sin perder ninguna idea?
evaluacion.texto: She was extremely tired on account of the fact that she had been working for long hours without taking any kind of rest, and she therefore made the decision to go to bed early.
opciones: She was tired after long hours without rest, so she decided to go to bed early.
She was tired, so she went to bed.
She was extremely tired on account of working long hours, so she made the decision to sleep early.
She was tired after long hours without rest, so she decided to sleep.
evaluacion.feedback: Solo la versión «tired after long hours without rest» conserva las dos ideas (horas largas sin descanso y acostarse pronto) con verbos fuertes; «went to bed» pierde información y la otra sigue siendo prolija.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El primer borrador era prolijo: repetía cada idea tres veces.»
evaluacion.texto: The first draft was ___: it repeated every idea three times. The final version is half as long, and nothing important has been lost.
evaluacion.feedback: Wordy describe un texto con más palabras de las necesarias; aquí, por repetir cada idea tres veces.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe un párrafo sobre una decisión y dos reescrituras concisas (230–290 palabras).
evaluacion.texto: Cuenta una decisión personal importante con conectores variados (admittedly, nevertheless…). Después copia dos frases largas de tu párrafo y escribe su versión concisa (Long version / Concise version).
evaluacion.respuesta: Last year I decided to leave my hometown and study in another city. Admittedly, the choice was not easy, because my family lives there and I had never lived alone. Nevertheless, I wanted a course that my local college did not offer, so I got to the point and applied. At first I was homesick, and the flat was small and noisy. However, I soon found friends, and my classes were better than I expected. My parents were worried at first, but they supported me in the end. Looking back, I am glad that I trusted my own judgement, although I still miss my mother's cooking. Long version: Due to the fact that I wanted to save money, I made a decision to work at weekends. Concise version: Because I wanted to save money, I decided to work at weekends. Long version: In order to be able to concentrate, I turned off my phone at this point in time. Concise version: To concentrate, I turned off my phone.
aceptadas: Two years ago I decided to change schools, and it was the hardest choice of my life. Admittedly, I was afraid of leaving my friends, and my parents were not sure either. Nevertheless, the new school offered music lessons that my old school did not, so I made up my mind and moved. The first weeks were difficult, because nobody knew me and the timetable was confusing. Even so, I soon joined the choir, and I am happy with my decision today. My parents now say that the move changed my life, and my old friends often visit me. Long version: Due to the fact that the bus was late every day, I had to make a decision to cycle to school. Concise version: Because the bus was always late, I decided to cycle to school. Long version: At this point in time I am in a position to say that I am satisfied. Concise version: Now I can say that I am satisfied.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen párrafo combina una decisión contada con conectores variados y dos reescrituras que conservan el contenido con menos palabras.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué quiere conseguir Tom con su correo?
repaso.texto: Dear Sol, thank you for your article. It is interesting, but the second page could be half as long. Several sentences repeat what the headline already says, and two of the stories add nothing. I suggest you keep the strongest example and delete the rest. You will lose words but not ideas. Best wishes, Tom.
opciones: To persuade Sol to cut repetition without losing ideas.
To ask Sol to replace the headline with a shorter one.
To ask for more examples that support the headline.
To say that the article is too short for the newspaper.
repaso.feedback: Tom elogia el artículo y pide recortar lo repetido conservando el mejor ejemplo: «You will lose words but not ideas».

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Una de las dos palabras sobra: es redundante.»
repaso.texto: The phrase future plans sounds natural, but the first word is ___, because a plan is always about the future.
repaso.feedback: Redundant señala una palabra que repite lo que ya dice otra: plan ya implica futuro.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «El borrador era prolijo, pero cada idea merecía conservarse.»
repaso.respuesta: The draft was wordy but every idea was worth keeping
repaso.feedback: Wordy but… contrasta la forma (demasiadas palabras) con el fondo (ideas valiosas): por eso se recorta, no se elimina.
aceptadas: Every idea was worth keeping but the draft was wordy

classes.objetivo: Redactar un artículo de opinión para la revista escolar con tesis, dos argumentos, concesión, referencia interna y cierre, y documentar una revisión.

ensenanza.en: An opinion piece in the school magazine opens with its thesis: I will argue that pupils deserve a say in the rules.
ensenanza.es: Un artículo de opinión de la revista escolar abre con su tesis: defenderé que los alumnos merecen voz y voto en las normas.
ensenanza.nota: I will argue that + oración anuncia la tesis; have a say in = tener voz y voto en.

ensenanza.en: I concede that pupils may not always choose wisely, but they respect the rules that they helped to write.
ensenanza.es: Admito que los alumnos no siempre eligen con acierto, pero respetan las normas que ayudaron a escribir.
ensenanza.nota: Concede that + oración reconoce un punto antes de responderlo.

ensenanza.en: A writer may take issue with a counterargument, but answering it fairly makes the piece more convincing, not weaker.
ensenanza.es: Un autor puede discrepar de un contraargumento, pero responderlo con justicia hace el texto más convincente, no más débil.
ensenanza.nota: Take issue with + sustantivo = discrepar de algo.

ensenanza.en: To persuade readers, build a compelling case with two clear reasons rather than five weak ones.
ensenanza.es: Para persuadir a los lectores, construye un argumento convincente con dos razones claras en lugar de cinco débiles.
ensenanza.nota: Persuade + persona: persuade readers, no persuade to readers.

ensenanza.en: As mentioned above, rules that nobody explains are rarely followed, so a clear reason will persuade more readers than a threat.
ensenanza.es: Como se mencionó arriba, las normas que nadie explica rara vez se cumplen, así que una razón clara persuadirá a más lectores que una amenaza.
ensenanza.nota: As mentioned above es una referencia interna: remite a lo ya dicho.

ensenanza.en: I revised my draft twice, cutting two repeated phrases and ending with one example to drive the point home.
ensenanza.es: Revisé mi borrador dos veces, recortando dos frases repetidas y terminando con un ejemplo para dejar clara la idea.
ensenanza.nota: Drive the point home = insistir hasta que la idea quede clara.

explicacion.titulo: Un artículo de opinión completo, paso a paso
explicacion.texto: Un artículo de opinión eficaz sigue un camino claro. Introducción con tesis (I will argue that…). Dos argumentos, cada uno con su frase temática y un ejemplo. Una concesión (I concede that…, Admittedly…) y la respuesta al contraargumento (nevertheless…). Referencias internas que enlazan el texto (as mentioned above, this argument, the former, the latter). Un cierre que retoma la tesis con otras palabras. Antes de entregarlo, revísalo: quita repeticiones, aclara referencias, recorta lo que sobra y deja una nota de revisión.

formula.texto: I will argue that pupils should have a say in school rules.
First, rules that nobody explains are rarely followed.
I concede that pupils can make mistakes; nevertheless,
as mentioned above, a clear reason can persuade them.
In conclusion, pupils deserve a voice.

filas.texto: I will argue that pupils should have a say.
First, rules nobody explains are rarely followed.
I concede that pupils can make mistakes.
In conclusion, pupils deserve a voice.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am agree that students should have a say.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I agree that students should have a say.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo, no un adjetivo: no lleva am; se dice I agree.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: As it was mentioned above, rules are rarely followed.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: As mentioned above, rules are rarely followed.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En esta fórmula fija se omite el sujeto y el verbo auxiliar: as mentioned above.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Leo planean su artículo de opinión para la revista escolar.

dialogo.texto: I will argue that pupils should have a say in the rules. That is my thesis.
dialogo.traduccion: Defenderé que los alumnos deberían tener voz y voto en las normas. Esa es mi tesis.

dialogo.texto: Good. But some teachers will take issue with it, so you need a counterargument and a reply.
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. Pero algunos profesores discreparán, así que necesitas un contraargumento y una respuesta.

dialogo.texto: I concede that pupils may choose badly. Nevertheless, they respect the rules they help to write.
dialogo.traduccion: Admito que los alumnos pueden elegir mal. Sin embargo, respetan las normas que ayudan a escribir.

dialogo.texto: That is a compelling case. And finish with one example to drive the point home.
dialogo.traduccion: Es un argumento convincente. Y termina con un ejemplo para dejar clara la idea.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué debe incluir Mia además de la tesis?

opciones.es: Un contraargumento con su respuesta y un ejemplo final.
Una lista de las normas que quiere eliminar.
Una queja contra los profesores que discrepan.

item.feedback: Leo le pide un contraargumento con su respuesta y un ejemplo para terminar («drive the point home»).

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase expresa la tesis del artículo?
guiada.texto: Every term the rules change, and nobody asks us. I will argue that pupils should have a say in the rules they live by. Some teachers disagree, which is understandable.
opciones: Pupils should have a say in the rules.
The rules change every term, and nobody ever asks the pupils.
Some teachers disagree with this, which is perfectly understandable.
guiada.feedback: La tesis llega tras «I will argue that»; las otras frases describen un problema y admiten una objeción.
guiada.pista: Busca la postura que el autor anuncia con I will argue that.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Admito que quizá no siempre elijan con acierto.»
guiada.texto: Pupils can make mistakes, and I ___ that they may not always choose wisely. Nevertheless, they respect the rules they helped to write.
guiada.feedback: Concede that introduce un punto que el autor reconoce antes de responderlo con nevertheless.
guiada.pista: Verbo de la familia de concession.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Como se mencionó arriba, las normas sin explicación rara vez se cumplen.»
guiada.respuesta: As mentioned above rules without explanation are rarely followed
guiada.feedback: As mentioned above remite a una idea ya expuesta y deja el resto de la frase intacta.
aceptadas: Rules without explanation are rarely followed as mentioned above
guiada.pista: La referencia interna abre la frase.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué hace el autor con la objeción de «some»?
practica.texto: Some will say that pupils cannot be trusted with rules. I take issue with that view. When pupils helped to write the phone policy last year, complaints fell by half, because people follow rules that they understand.
opciones: He states it and answers it with a concrete example.
He accepts part of it and adjusts his thesis accordingly.
He answers it with a general principle but gives no example.
He uses it as the conclusion of his piece.
practica.feedback: Enuncia la objeción («Some will say…»), discrepa («I take issue with…») y la rebate con el ejemplo de la política de celulares.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué aprendió la autora de la editora.
practica.audio: Our magazine editor read my draft aloud and stopped after the third paragraph. You concede the main objection, she said, and then you never answer it. I had thought that admitting the point was enough. She explained that a concession without a reply leaves the reader exactly where the critic left him. I wrote two sentences of reply, and the piece suddenly felt finished.
opciones: A concession needs a reply, or the critic wins.
A concession should be removed, because it weakens the thesis.
A draft should never be read aloud before it is revised.
An editor should answer the objections, not the writer.
practica.feedback: La editora le explica que conceder sin responder deja al lector donde lo dejó el crítico; con la respuesta, el texto queda completo.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la parte del artículo que representa.
pares: I will argue that pupils deserve a say.
I concede that some rules are necessary.
practica.feedback: Cada frase cumple una función: tesis, concesión, referencia interna o revisión.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué actitud adopta el autor ante el riesgo de que elijan una norma poco sensata?
evaluacion.texto: Every September the school publishes a new list of rules, and every September most of us read it once and forget it. I will argue that this happens not because we are lazy, but because we were never asked. Rules that pupils help to write are followed more willingly, because people defend what they have built. Admittedly, a pupil council may choose a silly rule. Nevertheless, a silly rule can be changed next term, whereas a rule that nobody respects protects no one. In conclusion, the school should give us a say, and this magazine should keep asking for it.
opciones: He admits the risk, yet thinks ignored rules do more harm.
He admits the risk, but thinks teachers would choose more wisely.
He thinks the risk decisive, so pupils should not be consulted.
He dismisses the risk, because a silly rule harms nobody in practice.
evaluacion.feedback: Concede el riesgo («Admittedly») pero lo compara con el daño de una norma que nadie respeta: una concesión con refutación.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿A qué se refiere «this» en la segunda frase del texto?
evaluacion.texto: Every September the school publishes a new list of rules, and every September most of us read it once and forget it. I will argue that this happens not because we are lazy, but because we were never asked. Rules that pupils help to write are followed more willingly, because people defend what they have built. Admittedly, a pupil council may choose a silly rule. Nevertheless, a silly rule can be changed next term, whereas a rule that nobody respects protects no one. In conclusion, the school should give us a say, and this magazine should keep asking for it.
opciones: To the habit of reading the list once and forgetting it.
To the decision to publish a new list of rules every September.
To the pupils' refusal to be asked about the rules at all.
To the change in the rules that the school introduced this year.
evaluacion.feedback: «This» retoma lo dicho justo antes: la costumbre de leer la lista una vez y olvidarla.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Un contraargumento respondido con justicia hace el texto más convincente.»
evaluacion.texto: The writer states the main objection and then gives a fair reply. A ___ answered fairly makes a piece sound more convincing, not weaker.
evaluacion.feedback: Un counterargument respondido con justicia muestra al lector que el autor ha considerado el otro lado.

evaluacion.consigna: Redacta el artículo de opinión con revisión documentada (250–310 palabras).
evaluacion.texto: Tema: el colegio quiere prohibir los celulares en los recreos. Escribe un artículo de opinión para la revista escolar: tesis, dos argumentos, una concesión con su respuesta, una referencia interna y un cierre. Termina con una nota de revisión que diga qué has cambiado (Revision: I cut…).
evaluacion.respuesta: I will argue that the school should not ban phones at break, because a ban solves the wrong problem. First, pupils use their phones to talk to friends who are in other classes, and this contact is the only chance they have to do so. Second, a ban teaches pupils to hide their phones instead of using them well. Last term, for example, my class agreed on a simple rule and complaints fell by half. Admittedly, some pupils spend the whole break looking at a screen. Nevertheless, this is a problem of habits, not of phones, and, as mentioned above, a rule that pupils help to write is easier to respect. Some teachers take issue with this view, but a sensible alternative would be phone-free zones, which persuade without pushing anybody. I also believe that the school should trust us more, because trust is the best way to teach responsibility. In conclusion, the school should give us a say and trust us to use our phones well. Revision: I cut two repeated phrases and replaced due to the fact that with because.
aceptadas: In my opinion, the school should not take phones away at break, because a ban would hurt pupils who use them sensibly. First, many of us talk to friends from other classes, and this is often our only chance to do so. Second, a strict rule would teach us to hide our phones rather than to control them. Last year, for instance, our class made its own rule, and arguments about phones almost disappeared. It is true that some pupils stare at a screen for the whole break. Even so, this is a question of habits, and, as noted above, rules that pupils help to write are easier to respect. A reasonable alternative would be quiet zones, where phones are allowed only for messages. Some teachers take issue with this view, but I think it is fair to ask them for trust. In short, pupils deserve a say in this decision, and the magazine should keep asking for it. Revision: I trimmed two long sentences and removed a repeated example.
evaluacion.feedback: Un artículo completo tiene tesis, dos argumentos, concesión con respuesta, referencia interna, cierre y una revisión documentada.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué opina Carlos de los dos argumentos de Sara?
opciones: The first is clearer, while the second still needs an example.
The second is clearer, while the first needs a counterargument too.
Both are equally clear, but the concession weakens each of them.
The first needs an example, while the second is already the strongest part.
repaso.feedback: En la nota, «the former argument is clearer than the latter» indica que el argumento citado antes es más claro y el citado después aún necesita un ejemplo.
repaso.audio: Dear Sara, your piece is persuasive, and the ending is strong. Two small things: the former argument is clearer than the latter, which needs an example, and the phrase due to the fact that appears twice, so please tighten it up. As mentioned above, I would keep the concession, because it makes you sound fair. Best wishes, Carlos.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Revisé mi borrador dos veces y recorté dos frases repetidas.»
repaso.texto: The deadline for the magazine was Friday. I ___ my draft twice and cut two repeated phrases before it went to print.
repaso.feedback: Revised alude al trabajo de revisión documentada: releer y mejorar el borrador antes de entregarlo.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Una concesión prepara la respuesta en lugar de debilitar la tesis.»
repaso.respuesta: A concession prepares the answer rather than weakening the thesis
repaso.feedback: Rather than contrapone lo que hace la concesión (preparar la respuesta) con lo que no hace (debilitar la tesis).
aceptadas: Rather than weakening the thesis a concession prepares the answer
